questions.q: What does ServiceNow call its underlying relational data model?
options: The Glide Data Model
The Now Schema
The Workspace Engine
The Flow Framework
questions.explain: The Glide Data Model is ServiceNow's term for its table-based relational data structure, including table extension and reference fields.

questions.q: Which of these is a form of logic that runs in the application layer, per this lesson?
options: ACLs
The Glide Data Model's table extension
Business Rules
The Next Experience
questions.explain: Business Rules are server-side application-layer logic that run on record insert, update, delete, or query.

questions.q: What's the relationship between Classic UI/UI16 and the Next Experience?
options: They are two completely different platforms with separate databases
Next Experience replaced the database layer entirely
Both are UI generations rendering the same underlying tables, forms, and logic — a presentation choice, not a different platform
Classic UI/UI16 only works with custom scoped applications
questions.explain: The UI layer is a rendering choice; both UI generations sit on top of the same data and application layers underneath.

questions.q: Why does this lesson describe ACLs, Flow Designer, and integration as "platform services" rather than a single layer?
options: Because they don't actually do anything on a ServiceNow instance
Because they only apply to the database layer
Because each one cuts across the database, application, and UI layers simultaneously
Because they are optional add-ons most customers don't use
questions.explain: ACLs, workflow, and integration all reach into every layer at once, which is why they're treated as cross-cutting services instead of one stacked layer.

questions.q: What does an ACL (Access Control List) govern?
options: Who can read, write, create, or delete specific tables, fields, or records
Which UI theme a user sees
How many instances a customer can provision
Which Business Rules run first
questions.explain: ACLs are ServiceNow's security rules controlling access at the table, field, and record level, enforced regardless of UI.
